CLASSIFYING BUYS/BUYS-vs-SUPPLY, tells 1-9 from prior runs all still stand: (1) single-venue print from a wallet that KEEPS the balance is directional; (2) same-block multi-pool sweep into one hop then forwarded to a shared sink ending at 0 is arb; (3) same sender buying one pool and selling another in the same second is two-leg arb - apply to SELLS too; (4) eth_getCode starting 0xef0100 is an EIP-7702 delegated smart account; (5) buy/sell COUNT is not buy/sell DOLLARS on a thin book; (6) a BUY can be fake - a pass-through router with balanceOf 0 filling someone else's order; (7) a buy from an incumbent holder may be a REBUY after selling earlier the same session - compare balanceOf to 24h/48h ago; (8) a buy is REAL new money when balanceOf at -1h/-6h/-24h/-7d/-30d is all EXACTLY 0; (9) 'N BUY / 0 SELL' on a single pool is NOT a bid - a round-trip buying venue A and selling venue B records as pure BUY on A and pure SELL on B, so ALWAYS sum both venues. TELL 10 (NEW, this run): A CLAIM/vesting vault that pays the same wallet and gets the full balance back within seconds is a DISTRIBUTION EVENT, not accumulation - and it can be measured. The definitive test is the recipient's balanceOf right after the receipt: if it returns to 0 and a DEUS Transfer lands in a pool in the same block, it was sold, full stop. Track the RATIO of claim-payout to pool price impact rather than the payout alone: here 91,566 DEUS cost the mark -0.933%, so ~$1.7k of notional moves this pool 1%. That converts a vague 'overhang' into an actionable distance-to-trigger. TELL 11 (NEW): DO NOT read a missing h1 as flat, and do not read an API 0-volume row as calm - VERIFY against the pool's own Swap logs. Aerodrome Slipstream Swap topic0 is 0xb3e2773606abfd36b5bd91394b3a54d1398336c65005baf7bf7a05efeffaf75b (3 topics, 4 data words) - and it must be given as the FULL 64-hex hash; passing the 4-byte selector 0xb3e27736 makes eth_getLogs return -32602 invalid params (or a clean zero, which would look identical to a dead pool). The deepest pool's last swap was 99 minutes before this run. Supply is NET INFLATION (7d: 37 mints / 201,697.86 vs 18 burns / 136,317.22 = +65,380.63) - never call a single unchanged read deflationary. Total supply this run 876,206,780.447562. The escrow Burn event on 0xA85A3879 (topic0 0xe08737ac48a1dab4b1a46c7dc9398bd5bfc6d7ad6fabb7cd8caa254de14def35, indexed[1]=owner, indexed[2]=tokenId, data = [amount, timestamp, escrowBalanceAfter]) tells you who just unlocked and how much - treat it as a LEADING indicator, because the operator of that position then chooses when to hit the book (here: 75 min later, all at once). Conversely, the escrow balance falling is NOT itself bearish until matched to a pool Swap from the same address. Measure impact from the POOL RESERVE move (balanceOf of the pool on the token, block before vs after), not from the swap event data alone - reserve delta / reserve = the true fractional depth used. TELL 13 (NEW): A LARGE DUMP INTO THIS POOL GETS ABSORBED IN THE SAME BLOCK. 319,562 DEUS produced -4.37%, but 137,397 DEUS of same-block buying took a third of it back and net inflow to the pool was only 178,969 DEUS. TELL 14 (NEW, 2026-10-24 06:12Z run): VERIFY RE-ACCUMULATION AGAINST THE POOL RESERVE MARK, NOT THE SIZE OF THE BUY PRINTS.
